text: The government may arrest and detain any person without telling them the reason.
A suspect has no right to a lawyer of their own choosing.
Anyone may be held in custody indefinitely without being told the charges.
Citizens are forbidden from sharing ideas or information in writing or in print.
Newspapers must not publish criticism of the government.
Defendants shall not be given an interpreter in court.
Public gatherings of more than five people are prohibited unless the police grant a permit.
Workers are not permitted to form or join trade unions.
Suspects awaiting trial shall be held in the same cells as convicted prisoners.
A person convicted of a crime cannot ask a higher court to review the verdict or sentence.
The prosecution may bring a second trial against a person who was already found not guilty of the same offence.
Police may use any means necessary to make a suspect confess.
The death penalty may be imposed for tax evasion and other minor offences.
Prisoners may be subjected to beatings and degrading treatment as a form of discipline.
Citizens may not leave the country without written permission from the government.
A foreign national living lawfully in the country may be deported immediately, with no chance to challenge the decision.
Security agencies may read private letters and tap phone calls without a court order.
All residents must follow the state religion and may not change their faith.
Public campaigns that encourage the country to go to war are permitted.
Only members of the majority ethnic group may vote or stand for election.
Minority communities may not use their own language in community life.
Children accused of crimes shall be held in the same cells as adult prisoners.
A girl may be married by her family without her agreement.
Births need not be registered, and a child may remain without a name.
During a state of emergency the government may suspend all rights, including the ban on torture.
Women may not give evidence in court or sign contracts without a male guardian's permission.
The Ministry of Finance shall publish its annual budget report by the end of March each year.
Income tax shall be charged at a rate of ten percent on annual earnings above the threshold.
Vehicles shall be inspected every two years to check that they meet emission standards.
The national flag shall be flown on all government buildings on Independence Day.
Applications for a fishing licence must be submitted at least thirty days before the start of the season.
Public libraries shall be open from nine in the morning until five in the afternoon on weekdays.
Every person who is arrested shall be told the reasons for the arrest at the time of arrest.
Everyone charged with a criminal offence shall be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law.

source: Prevention of Terrorism (Temporary Provisions) Act No. 48 of 1979, s.9(1)
text: Where the Minister has reason to believe or suspect that any person is connected with or concerned in any unlawful activity, the Minister may order that such person be detained for a period not exceeding three months in the first instance. Any such order may be extended from time to time for a period not exceeding three months at a time.

source: Online Safety Act No. 9 of 2024, s.12
text: Any person, whether in or outside Sri Lanka, who poses a threat to national security, public health or public order or promotes feelings of ill-will and hostility between different classes of people, by communicating a false statement, commits an offence and shall on conviction be liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years or to a fine not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees or to both such imprisonment and fine.

source: Online Safety Act No. 9 of 2024, s.16
text: Any person, whether in or outside Sri Lanka who with the deliberate and malicious intention of outraging the religious feelings of any class of persons by way of an online account or through an online location by words, either spoken or written, or by visible representations, insults or attempts to insult the religion or the religious beliefs of that class by communicating a false statement, commits an offence and shall on conviction be liable to imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding three years.

source: Online Safety Act No. 9 of 2024, s.11(c)
text: The Commission may issue notices to any internet service provider or internet intermediary to disable access to an online location which contains a prohibited statement by the end users in Sri Lanka or to remove such prohibited statement from such online location.
